clauses.text: The volumetric ratio of spiral or circular hoop reinforcement, ρ_s shall not be less than that indicated by the following equation: ρs = 0.12f′c / fyt and shall not be less than that required by Eq. (6.6.12): ρs = 0.45 (Ag/Ach -1)*(f′c/fyt)
clauses.notes:
Volumetric ratio (ρs) - (volume of spiral or circular hoop steel)/(volume of the concrete core it encloses)

Spiral reinforcement - a continuously wound helical bar used as transverse confinement in circular columns

Circular hoop - a closed circular tie used as transverse confinement

Eq. 6.8.6 - the formula, ρs = 0.12f′c / fyt

f′c - specified compressive strength of concrete

fyt - specified yield strength of the transverse reinforcement

Ag - the gross area of the entire cross-section

Ach - the core area of a concrete column measured to the outside of the transverse reinforcement. The cross-sectional area of the confined concrete core enclosed by the outer boundary of the spiral, hoops, or ties.

clauses.text: The total cross-sectional area of rectangular hoop reinforcement shall not be less than that given by the following equations
clauses.notes:
Rectangular hoop - a closed rectangular tie used to confine the concrete core in non-circular columns

Ash - total cross-sectional area of all legs of rectangular hoop reinforcement in one direction within a given spacing

s - Spacing of transverse reinforcement; The center-to-center distance between consecutive hoops, ties, or spiral turns

hc - the width or depth of the concrete core that is confined by the transverse reinforcement

f′c - specified compressive strength of concrete

fyt - specified yield strength of the transverse reinforcement

Ag - the gross area of the entire cross-section

Ach - the core area of a concrete column measured to the outside of the transverse reinforcement. The cross-sectional area of the confined concrete core enclosed by the outer boundary of the spiral, hoops, or ties.

Eq. 6.8.7 and Eq. 6.8.8 - two formulas that each set a minimum value for Ash; the larger result from the two equations must be used

clauses.text: Transverse reinforcement shall be provided by either single or overlapping hoops or cross ties of the same bar size and spacing. Each end of the cross ties shall engage a peripheral longitudinal reinforcing bar. Consecutive cross ties shall be alternated end for end along the longitudinal reinforcement.
clauses.notes:
Single hoop - one closed rectangular tie enclosing the column core

Overlapping hoops - two or more closed ties whose perimeters overlap to confine a wider core area

Cross ties - straight bars with hooks at each end used to supplement hoops and restrain intermediate longitudinal bars

Peripheral longitudinal bar - an outermost longitudinal bar located on the column perimeter

Alternated end for end - successive cross ties are flipped so their hooks engage opposite sides of the column, distributing confinement evenly

clauses.text: Spacing of transverse reinforcement along the length l_o of the member shall not exceed the smallest of (i) one-quarter of the minimum dimension (ii) six time the diameter of the smallest longitudinal bar and (iii) s_o = 100 + (350 - h_x)/(3). The value of s_o shall not exceed 150 mm and need not be taken less than 100 mm .
clauses.notes:
lo - the critical confinement length of the member; max of (max dimension of the column, 1/6th clear height of the column, 450mm)

clear height of the column - the height of the column measured between the top of one floor/beam/slab and the bottom of the beam/slab/floor above

hx - the largest centre-to-centre distance between laterally supported longitudinal bars

Governing spacing - the smallest value from the three limits controls the maximum allowable spacing

clauses.text: Spacing of cross ties or legs of overlapping hoops shall not be more than 350 mm on centre in the direction perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the member.
clauses.notes:
Cross ties - straight bars connecting opposite sides of a hoop to provide intermediate lateral support to longitudinal bars

Legs of overlapping hoops - the individual straight segments of adjacent overlapping rectangular ties

clauses.text: Note: In beam column joints where members frame into all four sides of the joint and each member width is at least three-fourths the column width, the spacing of transverse reinforcement shall be 150 mm within the overall depth of the shallowest frame member. For all other conditions spacing shall be S_0. Use hoops and cross ties in beam column joint.
clauses.notes:
Beam-column joint - the region where beams and columns intersect, subject to high shear and confinement demands
Four-sided framing condition - when beams frame into all four faces of a joint and each beam width is at least three-quarters of the column width, the joint is considered well confined
Spacing of 150 mm - the maximum permitted transverse reinforcement spacing within the joint depth under the four-sided framing condition
Overall depth of shallowest frame member - the dimension used to define the extent of the joint zone for the 150 mm spacing rule
So spacing - for joints that do not meet the four-sided framing condition, the calculated spacing so from clause (b) governs
Hoops and cross ties - the required form of transverse reinforcement within beam-column joints
